title: Prevalence of synovitis in pediatric patients with Haemophilia A in Germany and Austria
summary:
Children with hemophilia A suffer from synovitis (inflammation of the synovial membrane). However, the actual prevalence rate of synovitis in this patient population has not yet been adequately documented. The aim of this study is therefore to close this knowledge gap.
The prevalence rate of synovitis in pediatric patients with hemophilia A is to be determined as part of a prospective cross-sectional study in a multicenter design. The data collection is purely diagnostic. Standardized ultrasound examinations of the elbow, knee and ankle joints will be performed to assess joint health. This is supplemented by an orthopaedic joint test. In addition, three standardized questionnaires are used to collect further information on joint function and the patient's general state of health.

interventions.name: In paediatric patients with haemophilia A, the elbow, knee and ankle joints are examined at one measurement point using standardized ultrasound and clinical joint examinations. In addition, three standardized questionnaires are filled out.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
o Suffers from moderate or severe hemophilia A, also with inhibitor or joint surgery in the past
o Complete documentation of the severity of hemophilia, treatment history (last 12 months) and bleeding events (last 12 months), inhibitor status (at the time of enrollment in the study and in the medical history)
o Submission of written consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
o Patients suffering from other bleeding disorders that conflict with the research question
o Patients participating in clinical trials with investigational medicinal products
